### BoK Gate check (v3 — MCORCH Master Execution Protocol)

For each BoK suite in `docs/bok/<slug>/`, verify completeness:
```bash
for slug in $(ls docs/bok/ 2>/dev/null); do
  required=(00-index 01-mrd 02-brd 03-prd 04-frd 05-sdd 06-data-model 07-process-flow 08-quality-metrics)
  missing=()
  for doc in "${required[@]}"; do
    [ -f "docs/bok/$slug/$doc.md" ] || missing+=("$doc")
  done
  [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ $slug — BoK complete" || echo "⚠️ $slug — missing: ${missing[*]}"
done
```

## Rules

- **TypeScript errors → report immediately.** If there are TS errors, list them under ALERTAS. Do not start implementing new features until errors are resolved (unless the user explicitly asks to proceed despite errors).
- **Unhealthy containers → report with triage.** Suggest the fix command if known (e.g., `docker compose restart mcorch-vector-engine` for chroma).
- **Uncommitted changes → describe, do not commit.** Only describe what exists in the working tree; committing is the user's call.
- **Keep the brief tight.** No padding. No repetition of CLAUDE.md architecture. The user already knows the architecture — they need the delta: what changed, what's broken, what's next.
- **Pending Actions priority order:** CRITICAL (before first client) > NON-CRITICAL > Phase Zeta > Core v3 > Epsilon v9.
- **Knowledge Mesh numbers:** use `GraphRAG State` section from HANDOFF.md as the source. Do not invent counts.

> 8163	### Embedding Model
> 8164	`openai/text-embedding-3-small`, `dimensions: 768` (truncated output via OpenRouter).
> 8165	Schema: `vector(768)` — HNSW cosine index.
> 8166	
> 8167	### Embedding Pipeline (Autônomo — 2026-05-03)
> 8168	Três camadas eliminam intervenção manual:
> 8169	1. **INSERT trigger** — `trg_mcorch_embed_on_insert` (pg_net) dispara `embed-mcorch-node` assincronamente em todo INSERT onde `embedding IS NULL`. Nunca bloqueia o INSERT.
> 8170	2. **Post-commit hook** — `.git/hooks/post-commit` roda `node scripts/ingest-codebase.ts --quiet` em background após cada commit → re-ingesta AST.
> 8171	3. **MeshControlPanel** — UI bottom-left do MatrixPage: "Sync Embeddings" (`trigger-embeddings`) e "Refresh Mesh Stats" (`trigger-ingest`).
> 8172	
> 8173	### Comandos de manutenção da Mesh
> 8174	```bash
> 8175	# Verificar nós sem embedding (deveria retornar array vazio):
> 8176	curl -s "https://bcyvddsykvehvpwstlfa.supabase.co/rest/v1/mcorch_nodes?embedding=is.null&select=id,name" \
> 8177	  -H "apikey: $SB_SECRET_KEY" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'{len(d)} nós sem embedding')"
> 8178	
> 8179	# Backfill manual (Bun-native — requer .env):
> 8180	bun run scripts/backfill-embeddings.ts
> 8181	
> 8182	# Backfill de código-fonte nos nós AST:
> 8183	bun run scripts/backfill-node-content.ts
> 8184	
> 8185	# Re-sync AST completo:
> 8186	cd packages/gitnexus-core && npm run sync-mesh
> 8187	
> 8188	# Acompanhar re-ingesta pós-commit:
> 8189	tail -f /tmp/mcorch-ingest.log
> 8190	```

> 8195	
> 8196	When a video generation operation (Google Veo) times out or client disconnects:
> 8197	```bash
> 8198	# Via edge function (production):
> 8199	curl -X POST "https://bcyvddsykvehvpwstlfa.supabase.co/functions/v1/rescue-video" \

> 8201	  -d '{"content_id":"<uuid>","operation_id":"<operation_name>"}'
> 8202	
> 8203	# Via local script (admin/debug):
> 8204	source .env && bun run rescue.ts <operation_id> <content_id>
> 8205	```

> 8241	### Canvas State Architecture (Hybrid)
> 8242	
> 8243	```
> 8244	User interaction → ReactFlow internal state (positions, drag)
> 8245	                         ↓ (debounced 600ms)
> 8246	                   localStorage (positions persist across refresh)
> 8247	                         ↑
> 8248	Store (Zustand) ← runPipeline → orchestrate-content Edge Function
> 8249	     ↓ (status changes sync to ReactFlow via useEffect)
> 8250	ReactFlow renders visual status (idle/running/done/error/blocked)
> 8251	```

## 🤖 Claude *(03:04:04)*

Agora tenho a verdade material do loop. Antes de sintetizar, deixa eu cravar o quadro honesto que os dados mostram:

**O que os dados de produção (verificados agora) revelam:**
- **Geração: funciona.** 2 ciclos pagos do Autopilot (−22 cada, 06-23 e 06-24), artigos+LinkedIn+threads reais (Roborock S8, Geladeira Samsung).
- **Distribuição: TRAVADA.** 3 posts LinkedIn `queued` desde 06-23/24 com `published_at: null` — nunca publicaram. 4 cancelados. O cron de auto-publish não está entregando.
- **Receita: R$0.** 11 links de afiliado, 10 cliques (a maioria do domínio de teste `mco.test`), `revenue_cents=0` em todos. Links ML são `bare-product + matt_word` só.
- **Autopilot DORMENTE** (`is_active: false`) — não há conteúdo recorrente saindo.
- **Poluição:** 2 artefatos de teste de injection ("Ignore all previous instructions...") sentados em `content_library` como `approved`.

O gargalo real do primeiro R$ **não é gerar conteúdo — é distribuição + atribuição**. Vou rodar um workflow de diagnóstico material em 4 frentes paralelas pra cravar a causa-raiz exata de cada quebra e separar o que executo sozinho do que precisa da sua mão.

# agent-browser

Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP with
accessibility-tree snapshots and compact `@eN` element refs.

Install: `npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install`

## Start here

This file is a discovery stub, not the usage guide. Before running any
`agent-browser` command, load the actual workflow content from the CLI:

```bash
agent-browser skills get core             # start here — workflows, common patterns, troubleshooting
agent-browser skills get core --full      # include full command reference and templates
```

The CLI serves skill content that always matches the installed version,
so instructions never go stale. The content in this stub cannot change
between releases, which is why it just points at `skills get core`.

## Specialized skills

Load a specialized skill when the task falls outside browser web pages:

```bash
agent-browser skills get electron          # Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, ...)
agent-browser skills get slack             # Slack workspace automation
agent-browser skills get dogfood           # Exploratory testing / QA / bug hunts
agent-browser skills get vercel-sandbox    # agent-browser inside Vercel Sandbox microVMs
agent-browser skills get agentcore         # AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers
```

Run `agent-browser skills list` to see everything available on the
installed version.

## Why agent-browser

- Fast native Rust CLI, not a Node.js wrapper
- Works with any AI agent (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Continue, Windsurf, etc.)
- Chrome/Chromium via CDP with no Playwright or Puppeteer dependency
- Accessibility-tree snapshots with element refs for reliable interaction
- Sessions, authentication vault, state persistence, video recording
- Specialized skills for Electron apps, Slack, exploratory testing, cloud providers

## Observability Dashboard

The dashboard runs independently of browser sessions on port 4848 and can also be opened through a proxied or forwarded URL such as `https://dashboard.agent-browser.localhost`. Agents should stay on the dashboard origin: session tabs, status, and stream traffic are proxied internally, so session ports do not need to be exposed.

> 
> # agent-browser core
> 
> Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP, no
> Playwright or Puppeteer dependency. Accessibility-tree snapshots with compact
> `@eN` refs let agents interact with pages in ~200-400 tokens instead of
> parsing raw HTML.
> 
> Most normal web tasks (navigate, read, click, fill, extract, screenshot) are
> covered here. Load a specialized skill when the task falls outside browser
> web pages — see [When to load another skill](#when-to-load-another-skill).
> 
> ## The core loop
> 
> ```bash
> agent-browser open <url>        # 1. Open a page
> agent-browser snapshot -i       # 2. See what's on it (interactive elements only)
> agent-browser click @e3         # 3. Act on refs from the snapshot
> agent-browser snapshot -i       # 4. Re-snapshot after any page change
> ```
> 
> Refs (`@e1`, `@e2`, ...) are assigned fresh on every snapshot. They become
> **stale the moment the page changes** — after clicks that navigate, form
> submits, dynamic re-renders, dialog opens. Always re-snapshot before your
> next ref interaction.
> 
> ## Quickstart
> 
> ```bash
> # Install once
> npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install
> 
> # Take a screenshot of a page
> agent-browser open https://example.com
> agent-browser screenshot home.png
> agent-browser close
> 
> # Search, click a result, and capture it
> agent-browser open https://duckduckgo.com
> agent-browser snapshot -i                      # find the search box ref
> agent-browser fill @e1 "agent-browser cli"
> agent-browser press Enter
> agent-browser wait --load networkidle
> agent-browser snapshot -i                      # refs now reflect results
> agent-browser click @e5                        # click a result
> agent-browser screenshot result.png
> ```
> 
> The browser stays running across commands so these feel like a single
> session. Use `agent-browser close` (or `close --all`) when you're done.
> 
> ## Reading a page
> 
> ```bash
> agent-browser snapshot                    # full tree (verbose)
> agent-browser snapshot -i                 # interactive elements only (preferred)
> agent-browser snapshot -i -u              # include href urls on links
> agent-browser snapshot -i -c              # compact (no empty structural nodes)
> agent-browser snapshot -i -d 3            # cap depth at 3 levels
> agent-browser snapshot -s "#main"         # scope to a CSS selector
> agent-browser snapshot -i --json          # machine-readable output
> ```
> 
> Snapshot output looks like:
> 
> ```
> Page: Example - Log in
> URL: https://example.com/login
> 
> @e1 [heading] "Log in"
> @e2 [form]
>   @e3 [input type="email"] placeholder="Email"
>   @e4 [input type="password"] placeholder="Password"
>   @e5 [button type="submit"] "Continue"
>   @e6 [link] "Forgot password?"
> ```
> 
> For unstructured reading (no refs needed):
> 
> ```bash
> agent-browser get text @e1                # visible text of an element
> agent-browser get html @e1                # innerHTML
> agent-browser get attr @e1 href           # any attribute
> agent-browser get value @e1               # input value
> agent-browser get title                   # page title
> agent-browser get url                     # current URL
> agent-browser get count ".item"           # count matching elements
> ```
> 
> ## Interacting
> 
> ```bash
> agent-browser click @e1                   # click
> agent-browser click @e1 --new-tab         # open link in new tab instead of navigating
> agent-browser dblclick @e1                # double-click
> agent-browser hover @e1                   # hover
> agent-browser focus @e1                   # focus (useful before keyboard input)
> agent-browser fill @e2 "hello"            # clear then type
> agent-browser type @e2 " world"           # type without clearing
> agent-browser press Enter                 # press a key at current focus
> agent-browser press Control+a             # key combination
> agent-browser check @e3                   # check checkbox
> agent-browser uncheck @e3                 # uncheck
> agent-browser select @e4 "option-value"   # select dropdown option
> agent-browser select @e4 "a" "b"          # select multiple
> agent-browser upload @e5 file1.pdf        # upload file(s)
> agent-browser scroll down 500             # scroll page (up/down/left/right)
> agent-browser scrollintoview @e1          # scroll element into view
> agent-browser drag @e1 @e2                # drag and drop
> ```
>

## ☁️ Cloudflare — liberar `www.mcorch.com` público (track B)

**Objetivo:** visitante real + Googlebot abrem `www.mcorch.com/?p=<id>` sem "Just a moment…", mantendo o `/wp-json` protegido (o Skip por header secreto que já existe **fica**).

1. **Diagnostique primeiro (não chute):** painel Cloudflare → zona `mcorch.com` → **Security → Events**. Filtre por `Host = www.mcorch.com` e veja a coluna **Service** do bloqueio (qual componente retorna *Managed Challenge*). A lição do unblock anterior foi exatamente essa: o culpado costuma ser o **"Nível de Segurança" (Security Level)** desafiando por reputação de IP — não bot/UA.

2. **Aja conforme o que disparou:**
   - **Se for "Security Level":** Security → Settings → **Security Level = Essentially Off** (ou Low).
   - **Se for "Under Attack Mode" (⚠️ laranja no Overview):** **desligue** (ele desafia todo mundo).
   - **Se for "Bot Fight Mode / Super Bot Fight Mode":** Security → Bots → desligue o Bot Fight Mode **OU** configure *Verified Bots = Allow* (senão o Googlebot leva 403 e você some da busca).
   - **Se for uma Managed/Custom Rule:** crie uma **WAF Custom Rule com ação Skip** ACIMA dela, escopada ao público:
     ```
     (http.host eq "www.mcorch.com"
        and not starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/wp-json")
        and not starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/wp-admin"))
     ```
     → Skip: *All managed rules* + *Security Level* + *Bot Fight Mode*. Isso libera as páginas públicas e **mantém** `/wp-admin` e `/wp-json` protegidos.

3. **Mantenha:** SSL em **Full**, e a regra Skip do `/wp-json` por header `X-MCORCH-Publish` (o publish server-side depende dela — **não remova**).

4. **Teste após cada mudança** (aba anônima): `https://www.mcorch.com/?p=24` deve **abrir o post**, não o challenge. Para o Google: Search Console → Inspecionar URL → deve dar 200.

> Resumo: o publish (server-side, header secreto) e a leitura pública (visitante/Googlebot) são **dois caminhos**. Você só precisa abrir o segundo, sem tocar no primeiro.

> 5	// The canonical ecosystem asset registry (creative_assets). Every module (canvas-studio, hyperframes,

> 12	export function useCreativeAssets(kind?: CreativeAssetKind) {
> 13	  return useQuery({
> 14	    queryKey: ["creative-assets", kind ?? "all"],
> 15	    queryFn: async (): Promise<CreativeAsset[]> => {

> 18	        .select("*")
> 19	        .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
> 20	        .limit(300);
> 21	      if (kind) query = query.eq("kind", kind);
> 22	      const { data, error } = await query;
> 23	      if (error) throw error;
> 24	      return data ?? [];
> 25	    },
> 26	    staleTime: 30_000,
> 27	  });
> 28	}
> 29	
> 30	type StorageRef = Pick<CreativeAsset, "is_public" | "storage_bucket" | "storage_key">;
> 31	
> 32	/** Public bucket → direct public URL; private → null (use resolveAssetUrl for a signed URL). */
> 33	export function publicAssetUrl(a: StorageRef): string | null {
> 34	  if (!a.is_public) return null;
> 35	  return supabase.storage.from(a.storage_bucket).getPublicUrl(a.storage_key).data.publicUrl;
> 36	}
> 37	
> 38	/** Resolve a viewable URL: public direct, else a 1h signed URL (private buckets like video-studio-assets). */
> 39	export async function resolveAssetUrl(a: StorageRef): Promise<string | null> {
> 40	  if (a.is_public) return publicAssetUrl(a);
> 41	  const { data } = await supabase.storage.from(a.storage_bucket).createSignedUrl(a.storage_key, 3600);
> 42	  return data?.signedUrl ?? null;
> 43	}

## 🤖 Claude *(20:10:16)*

Now the architecture is clear (Lei 1):
- `index.html` is the **root** composition; it loads intro/graphics/captions as **sub-compositions** via `data-composition-src` (and those layer divs already have `data-start="0"`).
- captions/graphics/intro are `<template>`-wrapped sub-comps — which is the **correct** pattern for `data-composition-src` loading. So the lint error *"remove the `<template>` wrapper"* is **misfiring** (the linter evaluates each sub-comp file as a standalone root). Applying it literally would **break** sub-comp loading.

This matters for your real question. Let me walk the actual user journey in the editor to ground the recommendation — open the app, check the Assets tab, the Lint, and whether it plays:

## 🤖 Claude *(20:11:34)*

Now I have the full picture (Lei 1, materially grounded):

**Caminho do usuário — o que está acontecendo:**
- **Vídeo** abre o `mcorch-demo` = o **exemplo "warm-grain" da HeyGen** (gerado pelo `hyperframes init`), não um projeto MCORCH. Daí o nome genérico e o lint barulhento.
- **`hyperframes preview` hospeda UM projeto por servidor** (uma porta cada). "Workspaces separados" = projetos/servidores distintos. Hoje só existe `mcorch-demo`.
- **Design** já é um app separado (OpenDesign / `design.mcorch.com`) — não compartilha nada com o Vídeo.

**Realidade do lint (importante — não vou aplicar cego):**
- Os 3 erros **"remove o `<template>`"** são **falso-positivo**: captions/graphics/intro são **sub-composições** carregadas via `data-composition-src` pelo `index.html` — e sub-comps **devem** usar `<template>` (o próprio lint diz isso). O linter as avalia como "root" standalone. Aplicar o fix literal **quebraria** o carregamento.
- Os 3 erros **"missing data-start"** são reais e seguros de corrigir (add `data-start="0"` no div raiz de cada sub-comp).
- Os 22 warnings são polish (selector `[data-composition-id]`→`#id`, `pointer-events:none`, GSAP overlap).

**Minha recomendação:** não vale debugar o exemplo da HeyGen. O melhor "iniciar" é um **starter MCORCH limpo** — eu autoro um projeto 9:16 próprio, lint-clean e on-brand (reaproveitando nosso template `viral-short-9x16.html` que já renderiza), e ele vira o workspace de Vídeo. Design continua no OpenDesign.

> 8	
> 9	- `/product-launch-video` — a **product** URL or brief / script → 60-90s product launch / SaaS / promo video.

> 11	- `/faceless-explainer` — arbitrary text (topic / article / notes), **no URL, no website capture** → 60-90s faceless explainer.

(Plain captions/subtitles → `/embedded-captions`.)
